xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5165: Atlassian Rovo MCP v2 as an Overdeck skill pack (skills + MCP server wired into agents)

plan.title: Atlassian Rovo MCP v2 as an Overdeck skill pack (skills + MCP server wired into agents)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: Overdeck skill packs mount only skill directories, so a pack's MCP servers never reach agents. Atlassian's official Rovo MCP plugin (Jira and Confluence skills plus the https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp server) therefore cannot be used by Overdeck agents without hand setup, and its skills call tools the agent does not have.
narratives.Proposal: Add an `atlassian` known pack pinned to upstream commit 3be5562 with skills/v1 excluded and the four write skills opt-in. Teach the claude-plugin adapter to read a pack's https `type: http` MCP servers into the manifest, gate them behind a recorded operator consent (`mcp: true` written by add/update), and merge the servers of every selected, consented pack into the launch MCP file and the Codex server map in src/lib/mcp/agent-injection.ts after overdeck, role and project servers. For the atlassian pack, attach `Authorization: Basic base64(email:token)` from the PAN-5152 Jira tracker keys. Add a `pan doctor` Atlassian MCP row and document everything. Full detail, file/line references and before/after snippets: .pan/drafts/PAN-5165.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Running pan release stable or publishing to npm.
- Applying stdio or sse MCP servers from any pack, or expanding ${NAME} references in pack server definitions.
- Pack MCP servers for adapters other than claude-plugin (plain, deft-readonly, gstack-runtime).
- Delivering http MCP servers to the ACP host (acp, opencode) or provisioning MCP for ohmypi, kimi-code, muse, prime-agent.
- Driving the OAuth 2.1 sign-in for agents, storing OAuth tokens, or reading Atlassian service-account Bearer keys from tracker keys.
- Creating or using an eltmon/atlassian-mcp-server fork, or opening anything on the upstream repository.
- Dashboard UI changes beyond existing pack-row fields.
- Mounting skills/v1 or the repo's other client formats (mcp.json, gemini-extension.json, .cursor-plugin/).
- Editing src/lib/agents/runtime-command.ts.
- Showing a separate 'MCP servers (needs review)' Not-applied label for unconsented packs; the per-launch warning and the update preview cover it.

autoDecisions.summary: Merge pack MCP servers in src/lib/mcp/agent-injection.ts, not runtime-command.ts line 203.
autoDecisions.rationale: runtime-command.ts:203 is Codex-only and just spreads the map agent-injection returns; agent-injection already merges PAN-5061 project servers for every launch path (spawn, resume, recovery, planning, conversations), so one seam covers every harness that receives mcpServers.

autoDecisions.summary: Take the API-token header path: Authorization: Basic base64(jiraEmail:jiraToken).
autoDecisions.rationale: Atlassian's 'Configuring authentication via API token' page and the upstream README at the pinned commit both document this exact header, so the implementation checkpoint is resolved and the fallback is not needed. Admin enablement and token scopes are surfaced by the doctor row.

autoDecisions.summary: Apply only https type:http pack servers; stdio/sse stay Not applied; no ${} expansion.
autoDecisions.rationale: A stdio entry would execute pack code at every launch, which breaks the documented 'skill directories only' trust model; refusing ${} references means a pack can never pull an operator secret into a URL or header.

autoDecisions.summary: Require recorded consent (registry mcp: true) before a pack's MCP servers reach agents.
autoDecisions.rationale: Operators trusted existing commits under the promise 'MCP servers: Not applied'; consent written only by a confirmed add/update preview that listed the servers keeps that promise for already-trusted packs.

autoDecisions.summary: A pack contributes MCP servers when it is in the launch's pack selection (at least one skill on).
autoDecisions.rationale: It reuses resolveLaunchPackSelection, so the tools arrive exactly when the skills that call them are mounted, including per-skill and conversation layers.

autoDecisions.summary: Precedence: overdeck, role, project mcp_servers, then pack servers, lower pack id first.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue requires overdeck and role servers to win; putting explicit operator project config above pack defaults gives an override path for Bearer keys or OAuth-only setups.

autoDecisions.summary: Mark capture-tasks-from-meeting-notes, generate-status-report, spec-to-backlog and triage-issue opt-in.
autoDecisions.rationale: docs/SKILL-PACKS.md step 3 requires opt-in for skills that reach cloud write actions; these four call createJiraIssue/editJiraIssue/createConfluencePage/updateConfluencePage. The three read-only skills stay default.

autoDecisions.summary: Use the upstream atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server URL pinned to a 40-hex commit, with a documented fork-first exception.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names the upstream URL, no eltmon fork exists, the pack carries no Overdeck changes, and the commit pin already controls when upstream changes arrive.

autoDecisions.summary: Exclude skills/v1 through a new KnownPack.skillsExclude field; set no skillsRoot.
autoDecisions.rationale: skillsRoot is read only by the plain adapter; the claude-plugin adapter follows plugin.json skills and descends into skills/v1, where the copies drop out only by name dedupe and sort order.

autoDecisions.summary: Doctor row only when the atlassian pack is registered; endpoint probed only when its toggle is on at global or project level.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the SageOx doctor pattern and the issue's 'when the pack is enabled'; avoids a network call and a misleading warning for an unused pack.

autoDecisions.summary: Attach the header only when jiraBaseUrl is unset or a Cloud site.
autoDecisions.rationale: Rovo MCP is Atlassian Cloud only; a Data Center personal access token would always be rejected.

autoDecisions.summary: The header comes from the global Jira tracker keys (Settings / ~/.overdeck.env) for any project where the pack is on, not only tracker: jira projects.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-5152 stores Jira credentials globally (config.trackerKeys), not per project; the pack itself is the opt-in, and a project override (mcp_servers named atlassian) covers per-project accounts.

autoDecisions.summary: Pack server tools join --allowedTools like project servers (mcp__atlassian).
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches PAN-5061 behavior so agent tool calls do not stop at permission prompts; opt-in gating applies to the workflow skills, and roles with a tools: allow-list keep their own list.

autoDecisions.summary: Codex agents get the atlassian server only when the Basic header resolved; otherwise it is skipped with one warning.
autoDecisions.rationale: Codex uses a per-agent codex-home-v2, so the operator's OAuth sign-in is not available and a header-less server would fail every call; Claude Code reuses the operator's login by name and URL.

metadata.sizeJustification: One vertical feature (pack MCP servers end to end plus the atlassian pack that exercises it). The 24 files span skill-packs, skill-overrides, mcp injection, one conversation call site, the doctor CLI and docs; splitting into sibling issues would ship a pack whose tools never reach agents, or an MCP path with no pack to test it, which the issue's acceptance forbids.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. In src/lib/skill-packs/adapters.ts add the PackMcpServer type, readPackMcpServers(base, plugin) and mcpServerLabels(manifest) exactly as specified, add PackManifest.mcpServers?, and in readPackManifest (claude-plugin adapter only) set manifest.mcpServers to the applied servers and capabilities.mcpServers to 'declares servers Overdeck does not apply'. Applied = type 'http', url starting https://, valid non-'overdeck' name, string headers, no '${' in url or header values. Source order: plugin.json mcpServers string path (toRepoRelative), inline object (servers map or {mcpServers}), else <plugin root>/.mcp.json. No new imports outside node builtins; adapters.ts must not import skill-overrides/ or projects/. Add the six fixture tests from WI-1 step 5.

items.title: Given a claude-plugin fixture whose .mcp.json declares one https type:http server, readPackManifest returns it in manifest.mcpServers with headers {}, capabilities.mcpServers is false, and notAppliedLabels does not include 'MCP servers'

Given entries that are stdio, sse, http:// urls, contain '${TOKEN}' in a header, or are named 'overdeck', readPackManifest applies none of them and capabilities.mcpServers is true so notAppliedLabels includes 'MCP servers'

Given plugin.json mcpServers as a string path to a nested file and as an inline object, readPackManifest resolves the servers from that source; given invalid JSON it applies nothing and reports capabilities.mcpServers true
Given a plain-adapter pack with a .mcp.json, readPackManifest returns no manifest.mcpServers and keeps capabilities.mcpServers true
mcpServerLabels returns 'MCP server <name> (<url>)' for each applied server sorted by name, and an empty array when the manifest has none
